title: Dynamic fallback prioritization bug and post-incident hardening
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During a capacity pressure window on 2026-03-09 we observed a cascade of failures originating from the routing policy engine selecting an outdated fallback candidate pool (deprecated 8-bit quantized shards). The selected candidates generated higher tail latency and occasional truncated outputs for streaming calls. The router interpreted the truncated/timeout responses as downstream capacity failures and triggered deterministic cross-region retries, producing a retry cascade that amplified load and caused elevated 5xx rates for ~22 minutes.
impact_summary: Approximately 12% of user requests to hosted models in us-west-2 experienced elevated latency and 5xx errors between 03:14 and 03:36 UTC. Several enterprise customers reported degraded throughput and increased token costs due to retries. No data exfiltration or credentials compromise was detected.
root_cause: A race between policy refresh and on-the-fly prioritization allowed a stale policy snapshot to be evaluated against an updated candidate set. The stale snapshot carried deprecated candidate weights that prioritized a legacy quantized shard incompatible with current streaming handshake headers. Additionally, the retry policy treated 524/timeout variants as eligible for cross-region failover without respecting sticky route TTL, allowing oscillation.
timeline_highlights: 03:12 UTC - Autoscaler bounded available capacity due to sudden batch load spike (capacity event)
03:14 UTC - Router selected deprecated candidate set for fallback path (first anomalous responses observed)
03:18 UTC - Monitoring alerts for increased 99th percentile latency and 5xx rate; on-call engaged
03:22 UTC - Cross-region retry policy started routing to eu-west-1 and back causing oscillation
03:36 UTC - Mitigation: manual routing rule applied to pin to stable model family and disable cross-region retries; traffic normalized
03:50 UTC - Incident declared resolved; postmortem started
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Mateo Ruiz: Initial triage notes added. Root cause looks like policy snapshot staleness + retry semantics. Drafting reproduction steps.

2026-03-10 12:45 - Claire Nguyen (SRE): Dashboard links added; flagged that autoscaler metrics show a spike in tiny-batch requests that increased scheduling overhead. See dashboard: https://metrics.redwood.com/d/cluster/auto-scale?org=prod&from=2026-03-09T03:00Z
2026-03-11 15:05 - Aisha Patel (Eng PM): Prioritized hardening tasks into smart-routing initiative for this cycle. Requesting owners for two high-risk items.

2026-03-12 11:30 - Samir Banerjee (Runtime): Verified reproducer: simulating a policy refresh during candidate set update reproduces stale weight selection. Reproducer notes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing-tests/issues/58

2026-03-13 08:20 - Mateo Ruiz: Emergency patch (hotfix/ENG-49711-disable-cross-region-on-timeouts) submitted to disable cross-region retries for timeout-derived 5xx until proper TTL semantics are enforced. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/1423
action_items: Add strong policy versioning: attach monotonic policy_version to every evaluated decision and reject/migrate if candidate_set.version != policy_version (owner: Mateo Ruiz, due: 2026-03-20)
Enforce retry policy semantics: treat 524/stream-timeout as local-backoff only, do not trigger cross-region failover until sticky TTL expires (owner: Claire Nguyen, due: 2026-03-18)
Improve telemetry: emit candidate_id, policy_version, and candidate_version in routing traces for every request (owner: Samir Banerjee, due: 2026-03-17)
Add deterministic unit/integration tests: simulate concurrent policy refresh + candidate updates and assert no deprecated candidate selection (owner: Runtime test team, estimate: 3)
Canary rollout and chaos tests: deploy the policy refresh fix behind a feature flag and run canary with fault injection on policy refresh timing (owner: Aisha Patel, due: 2026-03-25)
Runbook updates: document manual mitigations to pin fallback candidate pools and guidance for rollback of retry policy (owner: SRE team, due: 2026-03-16)
Cost mitigation: add metric that estimates extra token cost from retries and alert when cumulative retry cost exceeds threshold (owner: Observability team, due: 2026-03-21)
acceptance_criteria: No routing decisions accept candidate sets where candidate_version < policy_version; all such decisions must be rejected/logged
Cross-region retries will not be triggered by streaming timeouts until sticky route TTL expires
Telemetry shows candidate_id and policy_version for 100% of sampled requests in production within 2 weeks
Tests cover the concurrent-update reproducer with deterministic outcomes and are part of CI
